signatures.description: Two or more tier-1 AI-overused abstract terms (delve, tapestry, leverage, seamless, pivotal, intricate, testament, vibrant, crucial, myriad, plethora, cornerstone, synergy...) within ~300 characters of each other. A single term is ordinary English; the cluster is the tell.
signatures.fix: Replace each with a concrete, plain-English word or cut the sentence; one of these words alone is fine, two in the same passage reads as generated.
signatures.example: AI: 'Delving into the robust tapestry of this intricate, vibrant landscape—a testament to a crucial paradigm shift.' Better: 'Here are three patterns from our analysis.'

signatures.description: Cautious epistemic preamble/disclaimer phrases inserted before a claim to soften it, including LLM-specific artifacts like a stated knowledge cutoff.
signatures.match: \bit('s| is) (important|worth) (to note|noting|mentioning) that\b|it could be argued that|as of my knowledge cutoff|needless to say
signatures.fix: Delete the preamble and state the claim directly; if a knowledge-cutoff disclaimer appears at all, remove it entirely.
signatures.example: AI: 'It is important to note that, as of my knowledge cutoff, the data suggests trends are moving upward.' Better: 'The data shows upward trends.'

signatures.description: Two or more stacked uncertainty qualifiers in one clause ('could potentially possibly', 'might arguably', 'may often typically help').
signatures.fix: Keep at most one hedge word, or commit to the claim.
signatures.example: AI: 'This could potentially argue that it may represent a shift. It may often typically help.' Better: 'This suggests a shift.'

signatures.description: 'Not just X, but Y' / 'It's not X, it's Y' rhetorical contrast pivot, including the two-sentence negation-then-correction variant ('X isn't Y. It's Z.'), used to manufacture drama out of a plain statement.
signatures.fix: State the single point directly without the contrast frame.
signatures.example: AI: 'This isn't just a tool. It's a paradigm.' Better: 'A tool for cleaning AI writing.'

signatures.description: Filler preamble sentence-openers, including SEO/travel-blog and generic filler phrasing, that add no information before the actual claim.
signatures.match: ^(Here'?s the thing:|At its core,|It'?s worth noting:|In essence,|Ultimately,|In the heart of|Let'?s dive in|Without further ado)
signatures.fix: Delete the opener; start with the actual point.
signatures.example: AI: 'Let's dive in: In the heart of the city lies a platform that streamlines workflows.' Better: 'The platform streamlines workflows.'

signatures.description: Inanimate nouns given human-verb agency to imply evidence without naming a source.
signatures.fix: Attribute the claim to a named source or state it as your own assertion.
signatures.example: AI: 'The evidence underscores the importance of security.' Better: 'Security matters because a breach cost us $2M in 2025.'

signatures.description: Verbose is-replacement verbs ('serves as', 'acts as', 'functions as', 'stands as') used instead of simple 'is/are'.
signatures.fix: Replace with 'is'/'are' for directness.
signatures.example: AI: 'This serves as a reminder that the platform represents innovation.' Better: 'This is a reminder: the platform is innovative.'

signatures.description: Formal academic connector words (Furthermore, Moreover, Additionally, In addition, Consequently, Notably, Importantly) opening a sentence, chained across a paragraph.
signatures.fix: Delete the connector or replace with plain flow; vary transitions.
signatures.example: AI: 'Furthermore, it is secure. Moreover, it scales.' Better: 'It's secure and it scales.'

signatures.description: Vague oversell verbs common in AI-generated marketing copy (unlock [your potential / the full power of], elevate, empower, streamline, harness the power of, supercharge, revolutionize), used without a supporting number or specific claim.
signatures.fix: Replace with a concrete outcome and number.
signatures.example: AI: 'We leverage synergy to transform your workflow and unlock customer potential.' Better: 'Reduced customer churn by 15% through personalized onboarding.'

signatures.description: Hedged claims attributed to an unnamed, unlinked source ('experts argue/believe', 'studies show', 'industry reports suggest', 'it's widely known', 'many argue').
signatures.match: \b(experts (argue|say|agree|believe)|studies show|industry reports suggest|research suggests|it'?s widely known|many argue)\b
signatures.fix: Name the source, date, and link, or cut the claim.
signatures.example: AI: 'Experts suggest AI will transform everything.' Better: 'McKinsey's 2024 AI report predicts 15-40% cost reduction.'

signatures.description: Extremely generic temporal-framing cliche opener.
signatures.fix: Delete and open with the actual problem or insight.
signatures.example: AI: 'In today's fast-paced world, staying competitive means...' Better: 'Last quarter, our slowest customer shipped 3 features in one week.'

signatures.description: Cliche phrase almost never used unprompted by human writers.
signatures.fix: State what the tool actually does with a number.
signatures.example: AI: 'Harness the power of automation.' Better: 'Automate your invoices in 30 seconds.'

signatures.description: 'In conclusion'/'In summary' used as a structural crutch to end a section.
signatures.fix: End on the point itself, or use a natural closer ('So:').
signatures.example: AI: 'In conclusion, the three points above demonstrate the value.' Better: 'These three facts matter because they shift the cost calculus.'

signatures.description: Forced numeric listicle title pattern (3/5/7/10 reasons/tips/ways).
signatures.fix: Use narrative structure, or let the list length be whatever it actually is.
signatures.example: AI: '7 Reasons Why Email Marketing Is Essential.' Better: narrative with embedded insight.

signatures.description: Stock SaaS marketing phrases repeated across thousands of AI-generated landing pages, including unsourced social-proof claims ('trusted by X companies') and generic positioning ('built for developers').
signatures.match: \b(unlock (your )?productivity|next.generation platform|boost your workflow|empower your (team|workflow)|seamless integration|elevate your (business|productivity)|trusted by \d+[k+]?\s*(developers|companies|teams)|built for developers)\b
signatures.fix: Replace with a specific product claim and metric.
signatures.example: Hero: 'Trusted by 10k+ developers. Elevate Your Productivity With Our AI-Powered Solution.' Better: 'Cut code review time from 2 hours to 15 minutes; used at Stripe and Figma.'

signatures.description: Disclaimer phrases that announce structure instead of embedding it naturally.
signatures.fix: Cut the phrase; let context carry the reference.
signatures.example: AI: 'As mentioned above, customer satisfaction matters.' Better: state the point once, don't re-announce it.

signatures.description: More than 2 em dashes within a single paragraph/section, a strong statistical AI-authorship signal.
signatures.fix: Convert most em-dash asides into separate sentences or commas.
signatures.example: AI: 'The system—built on modern architecture—provides—seamlessly—integration.' Better: split into short sentences.

signatures.description: Rule-of-three adjective/noun triads used as filler (X, Y, and Z) especially when repeated across adjacent sentences.
signatures.fix: Vary list length (2, 4, 5 items) instead of defaulting to three.
signatures.example: AI: 'Scalable, secure, and simple. Fast, reliable, and easy to use.' Better: vary structure and length.

signatures.description: Empty catch block that silently swallows an exception (JS/TS).
signatures.fix: Log the error and either rethrow or handle a specific failure mode.
signatures.example: AI: 'try { risky(); } catch (e) {}' Better: 'catch (e) { throw new ValidationError(e.message); }'

signatures.description: Bare or broad except clause that swallows the exception without handling it (Python), including the same-line 'except: pass' form.
signatures.fix: Catch specific exception types and log/handle each.
signatures.example: AI: 'try: db.execute(query) except: pass' Better: 'except IntegrityError as e: log.error(e); raise'

signatures.description: TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX comments left in code intended to ship, indicating unfinished scaffolding.
signatures.fix: Resolve the TODO or file it as a tracked issue and remove from source.
signatures.example: AI: 'if (true) { handleSuccess(); } else { // TODO: handle error }'

signatures.description: console.log/debug statements left in production-bound code.
signatures.fix: Remove or replace with a proper logger behind a debug flag.
signatures.example: AI leaves 'console.log(data)' inside a shipped component.

signatures.description: Dead/always-true conditional branch, a sign of unfinished or scaffolded logic.
signatures.fix: Replace the literal with the real condition.
signatures.example: AI: 'if (true) { handleSuccess(); } else { /* TODO */ }' Better: 'if (success) { handleSuccess(); } else { handleError(); }'

signatures.description: CSS `transition: all` animates every property including layout-affecting ones, causing jank; a common AI default.
signatures.fix: List only the properties you intend to animate (prefer transform/opacity).
signatures.example: AI: 'transition: all 0.3s ease;' Better: 'transition: opacity 0.3s ease, color 0.3s ease;'

signatures.description: Hardcoded credential-shaped string assigned to a key/secret/password variable.
signatures.fix: Move to environment variables or a secrets manager.
signatures.example: const apiKey = "sk_live_1234567890abcdef1234";

signatures.description: Comment restating an obvious one-line operation instead of explaining intent ('// loop through array', '// increment counter', '// create array').
signatures.fix: Delete restating comments; only comment non-obvious business logic.
signatures.example: AI: '// Loop through array\nfor (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {'

signatures.description: Placeholder comment indicating omitted/truncated code, signaling an incomplete file was shipped.
signatures.match: (//|#)\s*(\.\.\.\s*)?(rest of (the )?(code|file|middleware)|remains the same|add more (fields|logic) as needed)
signatures.fix: Ship the complete file with no ellipsis placeholders.
signatures.example: AI: 'function handler() { /* ... rest of middleware ... */ }'

signatures.description: Non-descriptive placeholder variable names (data, result, temp, tempVar, output) used for non-trivial values.
signatures.fix: Rename to what the value actually represents (e.g. userProfiles, paymentResponse).
signatures.example: AI: 'const data = fetchFromAPI(); const result = data.map(item => item.value);'

signatures.description: JSDoc/docstring @throws or behavior claim with no corresponding validation/error-throwing code in the function body.
signatures.fix: Verify the documented behavior actually exists in the implementation, or remove the claim.
signatures.example: @throws {ValidationError} documented but function body has no try-catch or validation logic.

signatures.description: Tailwind purple/violet-to-pink/blue/indigo gradient utility classes anchored to an actual gradient direction utility, the most common AI visual fingerprint.
signatures.fix: Replace with a brand-specific two-color pairing defined in tailwind.config, or drop the gradient.
signatures.example: class="bg-gradient-to-r from-purple-600 to-pink-600"

signatures.description: Raw CSS linear-gradient using the exact canonical AI-default purple/violet-to-blue/cyan/pink hex values.
signatures.fix: Use a brand-derived palette instead of the statistical-default purple/pink.
signatures.example: background: linear-gradient(135deg, #7c3aed 0%, #06b6d4 100%);

signatures.description: Frosted-glass transparency effect (backdrop-blur combined with a low-opacity white/black background) commonly overused on navbars and cards.
signatures.fix: Use a solid opaque background or elevation shadow instead of transparency.
signatures.example: class="backdrop-blur-md bg-white/10"

signatures.description: Inter used as the sole/default font family — the most statistically common AI-default typeface.
signatures.fix: Commit to a distinctive serif, geometric sans, or system font pairing instead of the default.
signatures.example: body { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; }

signatures.description: Unmodified Tailwind default-hue-band accent color (indigo/blue/violet 500-600), the historical shadcn/Tailwind UI default that AI models learned as 'good UI color', when no custom --color-primary token is defined nearby.
signatures.fix: Override with a custom brand color token in tailwind.config.js.
signatures.example: <button class="bg-indigo-500">

signatures.description: Default shadcn/ui zinc or slate gray palette used directly with no tailwind.config override, signaling an untouched template.
signatures.fix: Shift hue or lighten/darken the neutral palette in tailwind.config.js.
signatures.example: <div class="bg-white text-zinc-900">

signatures.description: rounded-2xl combined with shadow-lg applied broadly (buttons, cards, inputs) in either class order, an AI over-rounding default.
signatures.fix: Use smaller/varied radii (4-8px) and lighter shadows differentiated by element importance.
signatures.example: <button class="rounded-2xl shadow-lg">

signatures.description: Single colored 3-4px left border strip on card containers — the single most statistically reliable AI-UI tell. Context-dependent: blockquotes and callouts legitimately use a 3-4px left border, so weigh hits by where the rule sits.
signatures.fix: Differentiate cards via whitespace, background tint, or elevation instead of a colored left border.
signatures.example: <div class="border-l-4 border-indigo-500 rounded-lg p-4">

signatures.description: Emoji characters (including plain/heavy checkmarks) used as feature-list bullets or UI icons instead of a real icon system.
signatures.fix: Replace with monoline SVG icons from a consistent icon set.
signatures.example: 🚀 Fast performance\n⚡ Real-time updates\n💡 Intuitive design

signatures.description: Cubic-bezier easing with an overshoot value greater than 1 (bounce/elastic effect) on hover/micro-interactions.
signatures.fix: Use a deceleration curve like cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) for functional UI animation.
signatures.example: transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);

signatures.description: The exact same padding/gap utility (e.g. p-4 gap-4) repeated identically across hero, cards, and footer sections with no rhythm variation.
signatures.fix: Vary spacing by section importance (tighter for dense UI, looser for hero/marketing sections).
signatures.example: Hero, cards, and footer all using identical p-8 gap-4.

signatures.description: grid-cols-3 combined with three structurally-identical child cards (same depth, same class pattern, similar copy length) — the canonical AI landing-page layout.
signatures.fix: Use an asymmetric grid, 2/4/5-column layout, or vary card heights/content density.
signatures.example: <div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-6"> with three identical <Card> children.

signatures.description: A <button> whose only child is an icon/svg with no aria-label, aria-labelledby, or visible text — fails accessibility and hides intent.
signatures.fix: Add aria-label describing the action, or include visible text alongside the icon.
signatures.example: <button><Icon name="menu" /></button> -> <button aria-label="Open navigation menu"><Icon name="menu" /></button>

signatures.description: Generic placeholder/filler text used as shipped UI copy instead of task-specific content.
signatures.match: placeholder=["'](Enter text( here)?|Click here|Type here|Select an option)["']
signatures.fix: Replace with concrete, task-specific placeholder copy (e.g. 'First name (e.g., Jane)').
signatures.example: <input placeholder="Enter text here" />

signatures.description: Lorem ipsum filler text shipped in place of real content.
signatures.fix: Replace with real copy before shipping.
signatures.example: <Card>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet...</Card>

signatures.description: The canonical AI hero pattern: exactly two buttons reading 'Get Started' and 'Learn More' co-occurring.
signatures.fix: Use a single, specific primary CTA with product-relevant wording.
signatures.example: <button>Get Started</button> <button>Learn More</button>

signatures.description: All buttons in a file share the exact same filled-primary class combination with no outline/ghost secondary variant defined.
signatures.fix: Define outline/ghost secondary and tertiary button variants for non-primary actions.
signatures.example: Every CTA in the file is a filled blue button with no outline variant.

signatures.description: Second-tier AI vocabulary cluster of ordinary business-speak nouns/adjectives (cutting-edge, empower, streamline, innovative, showcase, landscape, realm, ecosystem, multifaceted, best-in-class, future-ready) that are individually common English words.
signatures.fix: Only treat as signal when 2+ distinct terms cluster in the same paragraph; a lone 'ecosystem' or 'landscape' is very likely legitimate usage.
signatures.example: AI: 'Our cutting-edge platform empowers you to navigate the ever-changing landscape of this multifaceted ecosystem.'

signatures.description: Bulleted list item with a bolded keyword followed by a colon, a mechanical rule-of-three formatting habit when the pattern repeats 3+ times consecutively.
signatures.fix: Flag only when the pattern repeats 3+ times consecutively in the same list; vary bullet structure/length instead of bold-keyword-colon for every item.
signatures.example: '- **Speed**: Faster processing.\n- **Scale**: Bigger capacity.\n- **Security**: Better protection.'

signatures.description: Function/method body that is only a placeholder (todo!(), raise NotImplementedError, bare pass, or a lone ellipsis line) shipped as if complete.
signatures.fix: Implement the body fully, or raise an explicit NotImplementedError tied to a tracked ticket instead of a silent pass/ellipsis.
signatures.example: def process_data(data):\n    # TODO: implement later\n    pass

signatures.description: Python function defined with a mutable default argument (a list or dict literal), a classic accidental-shared-state bug.
signatures.fix: Use None as the default and construct the mutable object inside the function body.
signatures.example: AI: 'def add_item(item, items=[]): items.append(item); return items' Better: 'def add_item(item, items=None): items = items or []; ...'

signatures.description: A clickable <div> given an ARIA role instead of native semantic HTML (button/checkbox/link).
signatures.fix: Use the native <button>, <input type=checkbox>, or <a> element instead of re-implementing its semantics on a div.
signatures.example:
Click me
->

signatures.description: Fire-and-forget async callback passed to .map() with no surrounding await/Promise.all, silently dropping rejections.
signatures.fix: Confirm the surrounding expression is not already wrapped in Promise.all(...); if it is, this is fine. If not, wrap it or replace with a for-loop with await.
signatures.example: users.map(async (u) => saveUser(u)); // unhandled rejections -> await Promise.all(users.map(async (u) => saveUser(u)));

signatures.description: Non-idiomatic camelCase abbreviation handling (e.g. loadHTTPURL instead of loadHttpUrl).
signatures.fix: Pick one abbreviation-casing convention for the codebase and apply it consistently; this is a style-consistency check, not proof of AI authorship.
signatures.example: loadHTTPURLFromCache -> loadHttpUrlFromCache (or keep full-caps consistently, per your style guide).

signatures.description: A single file mixes 'export default' and named 'export const' exports.
signatures.fix: Only worth flagging if the file's own export convention is otherwise consistently one style; don't treat this as a slop signal on its own.
signatures.example: export default function Button() {} \n export const ButtonVariant = {...}

signatures.description: Leftover DOM attributes or comments from AI web-builder tools (v0, Lovable, Bolt.new, GPT Engineer) shipped into production markup.
signatures.fix: Strip all builder-tool data attributes and generated-by comments before shipping.
signatures.example: ...

signatures.description: Raw CSS glassmorphism effect (backdrop-filter blur paired with a low-opacity white rgba background), the non-Tailwind counterpart of the utility-class glassmorphism tell.
signatures.fix: Use a solid opaque background or elevation shadow instead of transparency, or reserve it for one deliberate overlay element.
signatures.example: background: rgba(255,255,255,0.1); backdrop-filter: blur(10px);

signatures.description: Gradient headline text via background-clip:text, an AI marketing-page signature when paired with the default purple/blue palette.
signatures.fix: Only a meaningful tell in combination with the default purple/blue gradient palette; on its own it's a neutral CSS technique.
signatures.example: h1 { background: linear-gradient(90deg, #7c3aed, #06b6d4); -webkit-background-clip: text; color: transparent; }

signatures.description: Neon cyan/violet glow box-shadow on card/element borders over a dark background, a code-generator (v0/Cursor) visual trademark.
signatures.fix: Use a subtle elevation shadow in a brand-neutral color instead of a saturated neon glow.
signatures.example: box-shadow: 0 0 20px 4px #a855f7;

signatures.description: Pill-shaped badge above a headline using rounded-full plus small padding plus a tinted background utility combo.
signatures.fix: Pill badges are a legitimate UI pattern; only worth noting alongside other AI-default tells (purple/indigo palette, Inter, three-card grid) rather than on its own.
signatures.example: New above a hero headline.

signatures.description: Centered hero heading with a centered, mx-auto primary CTA button directly beneath it — the canonical AI landing-page hero layout.
signatures.fix: Only meaningful combined with other tells (three-card grid, purple gradient, Inter font); on its own, centered heroes are normal.
signatures.example: ...

signatures.description: Empty state rendered as a bare 'No results'/'No data' message with no explanation, illustration, or next-step CTA.
signatures.fix: Explain why the list is empty and offer a concrete next action instead of a bare status line.
signatures.example: Slop: blank page + 'No results found'. Better: 'You haven't uploaded a document yet — create your first one to get started.'

signatures.description: Vague, non-actionable error text with no stated cause or recovery path ('Something went wrong', 'An error occurred', 'Error!').
signatures.fix: Name the actual problem and give a concrete recovery step instead of a generic fallback string.
signatures.example: Slop: 'Something went wrong.' Better: 'We couldn't save your changes — check your connection and try again.'

signatures.description: Obviously fake mock data shipped in a final UI (Jane Doe, John Doe, User Name, $0.00) instead of realistic sample content.
signatures.fix: Replace with realistic sample data reflecting real names, amounts, and string lengths the product will actually show.
signatures.example: Slop: profile card showing 'Jane Doe' / '$0.00'. Better: a realistic example profile with plausible name and balance.

signatures.description: Indeterminate spinner class paired with generic 'Loading...' text and no skeleton or progress indicator.
signatures.fix: Replace with a skeleton screen that matches the final layout, or a determinate progress indicator where possible.
signatures.example: Loading...

signatures.description: A list/data render (`{items.map(...)}`) with no visible loading, error, or empty-state guard around it in the surrounding component.
signatures.fix: Only flag when the surrounding component genuinely lacks loading/error/empty branches — a bare match on `.map(` is not sufficient signal on its own.
signatures.example: {items.map(item => <Card {...item} />)} with no isLoading, error, or items.length === 0 check anywhere in the component.

signatures.description: Inline float/absolute positioning that visually reorders content without a matching tabindex, breaking keyboard navigation order.
signatures.fix: Keep DOM order equal to reading/visual order, or add explicit tabindex values that restore the correct keyboard navigation sequence.
signatures.example: A sidebar positioned with `position: absolute` appears first visually but is last in the DOM, so Tab lands on it last too.
